content.content:
=== V5__invoices_status ===
-- Invoices carry a payment status so a project's detail page can show UNPAID/PAID and mark one paid.
-- New invoices default to UNPAID; existing rows adopt the same default via the column default.
ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNPAID';
=== V6__invoices_amount_positive ===
-- An invoice must bill a positive amount — you cannot raise an invoice for nothing. Enforce it at
-- the DB level too, matching the server + front-end validation: rejects zero and negative amounts,
-- so no bad row can slip in through any path.
ALTER TABLE invoices
    ADD CONSTRAINT invoices_amount_positive CHECK (amount > 0);
=== V9__invoices_status_draft_default ===
-- Invoices now move through a lifecycle: DRAFT -> SENT -> PAID. A freshly raised invoice starts as a
-- DRAFT (it is sent later, which is what records an audit entry and unlocks payment), so the column
-- default becomes DRAFT. Existing rows keep whatever status they already hold.
ALTER TABLE invoices ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'DRAFT';
=== V4__invoices ===
-- Invoices: an amount billed on a project. Each invoice belongs to one project
-- (project_id -> projects.id), so a project's detail page lists ITS invoices and totals them.
CREATE TABLE invoices (
    id         BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
    amount     NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL
);
=== V14__invoices_amount_derived ===
-- The invoice amount is now DERIVED: it is the sum of the invoice's line items (Flyway V13), kept
-- in the amount column as a worked-out total rather than a figure typed by hand. An invoice with no
-- lines yet totals zero, so the "amount must be positive" rule (Flyway V6) no longer holds — a draft
-- can exist before anything has been charged to it. Drop that constraint; the total is still
-- recomputed on the server every time a line is added.
ALTER TABLE invoices DROP CONSTRAINT invoices_amount_positive;

## Summary

I implemented invoice cancellation (voiding) as a small, additive full-stack change:

**Server (OfficeFloor REST)**
- `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/InvoicesVoidLogic.java` — `POST /api/invoices/void` with an `{id}` body. Modeled on the existing send/pay logic: it only voids a **SENT** invoice (409 otherwise), flips its status to `VOID`, and records one audit line `INVOICE_VOIDED id=<id> amount=<amount>` through the `Audit` service ("note it").
- `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/invoices/void.POST.yml` — the one-file endpoint wiring.

**Front-end (new files only)**
- `features/invoices/voidInvoice.ts` — a `useVoidInvoice` mutation that POSTs and invalidates the shared `['invoices']` query key so the list re-reads the new status.
- `features/invoices/cancel.slot.tsx` — a contribution filling the existing `invoice.row` slot, rendering a `data-testid="invoice-cancel-{id}"` button (shown only while the invoice is `SENT`). Clicking it voids the invoice; the row's `invoice-status` then reads `VOID`.

**Why no DB migration / dashboard change was needed**
- The `invoices.status` column is a plain `VARCHAR(16)` with no CHECK constraint, so it already accommodates `VOID`; adding a constraint would have broken other specs that seed `UNPAID`.
- The dashboard "outstanding" total already sums only `SENT` invoices (`DashboardGetLogic`), so a `VOID` invoice automatically stops counting toward what's owed — confirmed by the second test (`$100.00`, excluding the $50 void).

Both acceptance tests pass and the front-end typechecks.
